extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients and institutional officials (PD/PIs, Contact PIs, Signing Officials, delegates), and eRA Commons users
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting Research Performance Progress Reports (annual, interim, and final) to NIH via eRA Commons, including required content, roles/permissions, timing, and public-reporting considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / Scope of the RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR is used by recipients to submit progress reports to NIH on their grant awards. Progress reports document recipient accomplishments and compliance with terms of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview of annual, final, and interim RPPRs and resources to help understand how to submit a progress report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual RPPR content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use to describe a grant’s scientific progress, identify significant changes, report on personnel, and describe plans for the subsequent budget period or year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual RPPR includes accomplishments, products, participants/collaborators, impact, changes/problems, and budgetary information (budgetary information not required on Final/Interim).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use as part of the grant closeout process to submit project outcomes in addition to the information submitted on the annual RPPR, except budget and plans for the upcoming year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final RPPR omits budgetary information and plans for the upcoming year but requires a concise public-facing Project Outcomes summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim RPPR rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when submitting a renewal (Type 2) application. If the Type 2 is not funded, the Interim RPPR will serve as the Final RPPR for the project. If the Type 2 is funded, the Interim RPPR will serve as the annual RPPR for the final year of the previous competitive segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data elements collected on the Interim RPPR are the same as for the Final RPPR, including project outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method (where)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no RPPR form available for download. Submit RPPR data through the eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links for each type of RPPR are accessed through the Commons Status tab. The Interim RPPR link will appear one day after the project segment end date (but before closeout). The Final RPPR link becomes available through the closeout module once the grant is eligible for closeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may initiate and submit RPPRs (roles & delegation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the project director/principal investigator (PD/PI) or their PD/PI delegate can initiate RPPRs. For multi-PD/PI grants only the Contact PI or the Contact PD/PI’s delegate can initiate the RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing Officials typically submit the annual RPPR, but may delegate preparation (Delegate Progress Report) to any PD/PI within the organization on behalf of the Contact PD/PI. A PI can delegate 'Progress Report' to any eRA Commons user with the Assistant (ASST) role to prepare RPPRs. However, only a Signing Official (SO) or PI (if delegated Submit by the SO) are allowed to submit the Annual, Interim, and Final RPPRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to complete (process guidance & documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the instructions in the RPPR User Guide to submit the RPPR, Interim RPPR or Final RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The User Guide includes instructions for submitting RPPRs in eRA Commons, completing the web-based forms, and what information is required. Instructions for completing the scientific portion are in Chapters 6 and 7. Additional resources: RPPR Instruction Guide (PDF), Screen Shots of the R01-like RPPR (PDF), Guide to Categorizing Products in RPPR's Sec. C (PDF), RPPR Online Help, and sample project outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR due dates (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual and closeout RPPRs have defined due dates relative to the budget period or performance end date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNAP RPPRs are due ~45 days before the next budget period start date; Non-SNAP RPPRs are due ~60 days before the next budget period start date. Multi-year funded (MYF) RPPRs are due annually on or before the anniversary of the budget/project period start date. Interim and Final RPPR due dates: 120 days from period of performance end date for the competitive segment. Exact start date for a specific award may be found in grants status in eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accomplishments section elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on what was done under the award, addressing specific prompts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions to address: What were the major goals and objectives of the project? What was accomplished under these goals? What opportunities for training and professional development did the project provide? How were the results disseminated to communities of interest? What do you plan to do during the next reporting period to accomplish the goals and objectives?

rubrics_metrics.name: Products (Sec. C) content
rubrics_metrics.description: List and categorize tangible and intangible products resulting from the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include publications, conference papers, and presentations; website(s) or other Internet site(s); technologies or techniques; inventions, patent applications, and/or licenses; and other products such as data or databases, physical collections, audio or video products, software, models, educational aids or curricula, instruments or equipment, research material, interventions (e.g., clinical or educational), or new business creation. See 'Guide to Categorizing Products in RPPR's Sec. C' for categorization guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants and Other Collaborating Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Report participants and collaborating organizations involved with the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details on personnel participation and collaborations as requested in the RPPR web forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the impact of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists 'Impact' as a required RPPR element; use this section to summarize outcomes, significance, and influence of the work on the field or target communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes/Problems (when required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report significant changes or problems affecting the project and actions taken or planned to address them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements include: changes in approach and reasons for change; actual or anticipated problems or delays and actions or plans to resolve them; changes that have a significant impact on expenditures; significant changes in use or care of human subjects, vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents. Note: Changes/Problems is not required for Final or Interim RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary information inclusion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgetary information is requested on the RPPR but has specific exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgetary Information is not required for Final or Interim RPPRs (but is part of Annual RPPR content).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Outcomes (Final & Interim requirement and public language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise summary of the outcomes or findings of the award, written for the general public in clear and comprehensible language, without including any proprietary, confidential information or trade secrets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Outcomes are required on Final and Interim RPPRs. Note that project outcome information will be made public in NIH RePORTER — do not include proprietary/confidential information or trade secrets. See 'Sample Project Outcomes Summary - RPPR' for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality / public posting constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include proprietary, confidential information, or trade secrets in RPPR Project Outcomes because information will be public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit warning tied to Project Outcomes: project outcome information will be made public in NIH RePORTER; craft language accordingly.
